answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable reputation thread. Before trading, an agent must stake a refundable deposit and finish auditable tasks that peers can check. One fake identity is cheap, but building a credible thread for hundreds of fakes is expensive and slow. Like yarrow spreading only where roots take hold, reputation grows gradually and cannot be copied instantly. A crystal-clear trail of stake, work, and peer checks exposes fake clusters, letting the network freeze suspects and slash deposits before they distort prices or votes.
